name: shiftwork_clock_in
title: Shift work: clock in
description: Shift-work clock-in: validate the checkpoint against the checkpoint schema and return the brief of ONE unit — {unit, role, invariants, handoff, do_not, files} — to hand to the agent you spawn, verbatim. Call it once per unit, right before spawning; use shiftwork_plan first to see the `ready` batch when several units are to run at once, and shiftwork_clock_out, not this tool, when a unit finishes. The unit briefed is plan.cursor, or `unit_id` when given; either way it must be in shiftwork_plan's `ready` — a done or dropped cursor, a cursor whose dependencies have not run, or a `unit_id` naming no unit answers {"result": "error", "reason": "unit <id> is not ready; ready is <a, b>"}, and the batch view's own refusals (cycle, unknown dependency, unreadable checkpoint) pass through verbatim. The other outcomes, never exceptions: `escalate` when handoff.open_questions is non-empty (stop and ask the user) or when the cursor names no unit, `success` when every unit is done or dropped, `error` when the checkpoint fails validation. It never moves plan.cursor; clock_out does. What it WRITES: on result=brief, and only then, one line {event: brief, ts, unit, role} appended to <checkpoint>.log.jsonl — best-effort, so a log it cannot write costs the brief nothing. That line is what later lets clock_out accept the unit while the cursor is elsewhere and sets `briefed` on its accounting line. The checkpoint file itself is never modified. See docs/shiftwork.md.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Path to the shift-work checkpoint JSON file (by convention .shiftwork/checkpoint.json in the repo the job works on), absolute or relative to the server's working directory. The same file shiftwork_plan, shiftwork_clock_in and shiftwork_clock_out take; it must validate against assets/schemas/shiftwork-checkpoint.json.

unit_id.title: Unit Id
unit_id.description: The unit to brief instead of plan.cursor; it must be in shiftwork_plan's `ready` for this checkpoint. Omit it, or pass null, to brief the cursor unit.

result.description: `brief` (the unit is yours to spawn), `escalate` (stop and ask: see `reason` and `open_questions`), `success` (every unit done or dropped), or `error` with `reason`.

unit.description: The plan.units entry briefed: id, role, status, depends_on and its own fields.

role.description: The unit's role, the key job.roles may bind models to.

invariants.description: job.constraints: what every unit must keep true.

handoff.description: The checkpoint's handoff block: next_action, open_questions, do_not, notes.

files.description: state.artifacts: the files the job has produced so far.

open_questions.description: With result `escalate`: the questions the orchestrator must put to the user before any unit runs.

reason.description: With result `escalate`, `success` or `error`: one sentence saying why.
